message:
haven't got your saves from [tokyo](kebi://area/jp/tokyo) yet so i'm going off what i know, but here are some solid picks depending on what kind of night you want.

if you're after something iconic and you can get a seat, [Sukiyabashi Jiro](kebi://venue/d0d9936d-5eb7-4fea-8b9a-e9c517779e62) in Ginza is the one. that's the [sushi](kebi://venue/4a998fba-adc2-471a-a2fd-cd86cc33a333) counter most people only dream about. realistically though, it books out months ahead, so tonight is a long shot unless you already have a reservation.

same story with Sushi Saito Azabudai, another serious omakase counter, and [Narisawa](kebi://venue/e7b44b05-ab76-4a71-bb81-3cc243575088) in Minamiaoyama, which is the place for innovative Japanese cuisine with a nature-forward tasting menu. both are worth planning ahead for.

for tonight without a reservation, [Florilège](kebi://venue/56ae026a-1f8c-49ea-b71b-d4704b1b3779) in Toranomon is a strong pick. it's French-Japanese, one michelin star, and they sometimes have counter seats available on the day. worth calling ahead.

what would help me narrow this down: what are you feeling, sushi, something more casual, a particular part of the city? and are you solo or with people? tokyo is huge and the right answer really depends on which direction you want to go.
